I farm with a wheat-maize system, so I will keep most of my land in that rotation because it fits my water access, my experience, and the local conditions in Quzhou County. I have only a 10.1 mu farm and a two-person household, so I will keep the plan simple and labor-efficient. I will put 7.1 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 3.0 mu in cotton because I already know how to manage it and it helps me spread price and weather risk across crops. Since I have well irrigation, I will not farm too conservatively on fertilizer or water, but at my age I also do not want a management plan that is too intensive or complicated. For wheat I will use improved seed, stable fertilizer, and several irrigations to secure grain formation. For maize I will use hybrid seed and keep tillage light after wheat to save time and hold moisture. For cotton I will stay with a moderate area, use a fuller potassium program, and irrigate enough to support boll setting without making the whole farm too labor-heavy.
